title: Navimower 0.5.0-beta10

## Zone-constrained current-cycle trail

Field testing on H2 showed that distance-based gap guards are the wrong model
for Navimow retained trail geometry. Sparse vendor points may legitimately be
many metres apart. While mowing, the MQTT/live trail looked complete, but after
Dock the published vendor artifact could lose large parts of the visible swath
because 5 m / 15..30 m distance rules split the retained route into many pieces.

The captured Yard2 case still retained 461 raw vendor points at Dock, but the
gap guard had created 34 breaks.

### Raw vendor points are retained

VendorTrailStore no longer removes or permanently fragments current-cycle raw
vendor points based on the distance between consecutive samples.

A Dock transition, HA restart or sparse compressed vendor response therefore
cannot erase a valid in-zone trail merely because two retained samples are far
apart.

### Segment safety follows the zone polygon

At an artifact checkpoint, each straight edge between consecutive retained
vendor points is validated against that zone's actual map polygon.

- the edge may remain inside the zone;
- it may run up to **1 m** outside the polygon boundary to tolerate normal map /
  GNSS / edge-mowing offsets;
- the complete edge is checked, not only its two endpoints;
- this matters for concave zones, where two valid in-zone endpoints can still
  form a bad shortcut across a building or unmapped cut-out;
- if an edge leaves the allowed polygon envelope, only that edge is split;
  the raw vendor points on both sides stay stored.

There is no normal runtime 5 m, 15 m or 30 m point-spacing rule anymore.
The old adaptive distance guard remains only as a cold/test fallback when map
geometry is genuinely unavailable.

### Live tail

VendorTrailStore's supplemental live tail no longer creates a segment break just
because consecutive same-zone cutting points are more than 5 m apart. When the
zone polygon is available it uses the same 1 m polygon-constrained edge check.

### Migration

The render guard version advances to v3. Existing v1/v2 artifacts are rebuilt
with the zone polygon at the next lifecycle checkpoint, while their retained raw
vendor point arrays stay intact.

No Map Card update is required. Navimower Map Card 0.4.0-beta7 remains the
matching frontend.

Scheduler V2 from 0.5.0-beta9 is unchanged.
